hypothesis: Wiring /demerzel harvest and /demerzel compound as a single scheduled pair will prevent the input-staleness drift that produced Discussion #242, by guaranteeing the compound cycle never reads state/evolution/ that is older than the most recent harvest pass.

plan.description: Schedule harvest at 13:17 UTC Friday, compound at 13:47 UTC Friday — 30-minute gap matching the existing skill-doc recommendation. Document the dependency in both skill files so the pair cannot be split inadvertently.
plan.success_criteria: After two consecutive Fridays, state/evolution/ has at least one new file or updated entry per cycle; no compound run produces a static-inventory output.
risks: Harvest may itself be incomplete — would mask the drift problem rather than solve it
Cron permissions — scheduler may not have repo write access on the runner

check.evidence: Never executed: no compound schedule exists, and the Friday 13:17 UTC job (streeling-daily.yml) is a read-only harvest to Discussions with contents: read. It cannot write state/evolution/. state/evolution/*.evolution.json has gone seven Fridays without a commit (last 2026-07-29). The premise was also wrong about who produces evolution entries: git history shows every entry committed since July was recorded by the working session that shipped the change (e.g. 'state(afk): record ...', #873-#884), not by a harvest pass.

act.rationale: A scheduled /demerzel harvest + /demerzel compound pair is a recurring LLM spend. The owner has asked to minimise metered model consumption, and the pair targets a producer that does not exist in that form. The failure it was meant to prevent (compounding on stale input) is now detected by compound Step 0, which reads commit age since #1066, and by staleness-detection-policy 1.3.0, which classes the evolution log as live state.
next_steps: If evolution metrics need a scheduled refresh, prefer a deterministic producer (for example counting commits and PRs that reference each artifact path) over a scheduled LLM run. Open a new PDCA only once a consumer needs it: governance-quality-trend is that consumer and is in check.
